record.context_brief: Parabolic coefficient identification from interior-time snapshots.
record.original_question: Let Omega be a bounded connected open subset of R^2, let T > 0, and consider the parabolic initial-boundary value problem u_t - div(a grad u) = f in Omega x (0, T) with u = 0 on ∂Omega x (0, T) and on Omega x {0}, where a = a(x) is a time-independent scalar coefficient satisfying K^(-1) <= a(x) <= K. If f is known on all of Omega x (0, T) and u(x, t) is known for all x in Omega at one or more fixed times t > 0, is the coefficient a uniquely determined?

evidence.quote: Problem 7.1 (Parabolic inverse problem). Let n = 2. Given f on all of Ω × (0, T), and given u(x, t) for all x ∈ Ω and for one or more fixed values of t > 0, is a uniquely determined?
The problem however maintains its interest in any dimension, and is still open in general.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a bounded connected open set, let $T > 0$, and fix a constant $K \geq 1$. Consider scalar coefficients $a : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ that are measurable and time-independent and satisfy
$$K^{-1} \leq a(x) \leq K \quad \text{for almost every } x \in \Omega.$$
For a given source $f$ on $\Omega \times (0,T)$, let $u = u_a$ denote the (weak) solution of the parabolic initial-boundary value problem
$$\begin{cases} u_t - \operatorname{div}(a\,\nabla u) = f & \text{in } \Omega \times (0,T), \\ u = 0 & \text{on } \partial \Omega \times (0,T), \\ u(\cdot,0) = 0 & \text{in } \Omega. \end{cases}$$
Suppose that $f$ is known on all of $\Omega \times (0,T)$ and that, for one or finitely many fixed times $t_1, \dots, t_N \in (0,T)$, the snapshots $u(x, t_j)$ are known for every $x \in \Omega$. Is the coefficient $a$ uniquely determined by this data? That is, do $u_{a_1}(\cdot, t_j) = u_{a_2}(\cdot, t_j)$ for $j = 1, \dots, N$ (with the same $f$) imply $a_1 = a_2$ in $\Omega$?
artifact.status_search_result: The general uniqueness question for recovering a time-independent diffusion coefficient in a 2D parabolic equation from interior snapshots at finitely many times is stated as still open. Related results in the literature handle special situations (e.g., recovering a zeroth-order potential rather than the divergence-form diffusion, or using Carleman estimates with positivity assumptions on initial data, or boundary measurements over time intervals), but no complete uniqueness result for the divergence-form coefficient $a(x)$ from one or finitely many full interior time snapshots appears to be established.

status_evidence.title: Inverse parabolic problem with initial data by a single measurement
status_evidence.snippet: determining a spatially varying coefficient of zeroth-order term ... by a single measurement of Dirichlet data on an arbitrarily chosen subboundary
status_evidence.claim: Available single-measurement uniqueness results address zeroth-order coefficients with boundary data, not the divergence-form diffusion coefficient with interior snapshots.

status_evidence.title: Inverse parabolic problems by Carleman estimates with data taken at initial or final time moment of observation
status_evidence.snippet: determining a zeroth-order spatially varying coefficient by extra data of solution including measurements in the domain at a single time (t0 = 0 or t0 = T)
status_evidence.claim: Existing snapshot-based uniqueness/stability theorems via Carleman estimates apply to lower-order coefficients, not to the principal diffusion coefficient in divergence form.
